title: The Process of Budget Making: Sources of Revenue, Expenditure Management and Management of Public Debt
outcomes: Describe the Union budget cycle — preparation, presentation and enactment, execution — including the Annual Financial Statement (Article 112), the budget documents, the Finance and Appropriation Bills, guillotine and cut motions.

Classify government receipts (revenue: tax and non-tax; capital: debt and non-debt) and expenditure (revenue and capital), and name the bodies that administer them (CBDT, CBIC, Department of Expenditure).
Compute revenue deficit, fiscal deficit and primary deficit, and interpret what each tells us.
Explain public debt management in India — objectives, institutions (RBI's IDMD, Department of Economic Affairs, PDMC), FRBM Act, 2003 — and the three government accounts.

meta.exam_tip: Deficit computations appear in almost every attempt — learn the three formulas cold and remember that recoveries of loans and disinvestment are NON-debt capital receipts (they reduce the fiscal deficit) while borrowings are not counted. Also expect fact MCQs: 1 February, 75 days, 14 days, guillotine, Article 112, Article 266(1).

concepts.title: Introduction — what a budget is and why it is needed
body: Governments defend borders, keep law and order, provide public goods and run welfare programmes. All of this needs money, and the budget is the main policy instrument for raising and directing it.

Budgeting is needed because resources are limited: they must be allocated for maximum social welfare, reallocated to declared priorities, used to redistribute income and wealth, to reduce economic fluctuations, to raise real GDP sustainably and to narrow regional gaps.

A government budget is a statement of where the money will come from and where it will go: estimates of receipts and expenditure for the coming year and how any gap will be financed, along with projections for agriculture, industry and services. It is the most complete report of government finances. States and local bodies prepare their own budgets; this unit deals with the Union budget.
concepts.analogy: A household budget lists salary and other income against rent, food and fees, and plans a loan if needed. The Union budget is the same exercise for 140 crore people.
concepts.work: Every year after 1 February, CA firms publish budget analyses and clients ask what the budget means for them — the starting point is reading the receipts and expenditure statements correctly.

concepts.title: The process of budget making
body: The Ministry of Finance prepares the budget in consultation with NITI Aayog and the other ministries. It must be passed by both Houses of Parliament before the financial year begins (1 April to 31 March).

The word "budget" does not appear in the Constitution. Article 112 requires the President to place before both Houses, for every financial year, an estimate of what the Government of India expects to receive and to spend — this is called the Annual Financial Statement (AFS).

Three stages: (i) preparation, (ii) presentation and enactment, (iii) execution. Two kinds of activity: the administrative process (preparing the budget and documents with stakeholders) and the legislative process (Parliament discussing and passing it).

Work starts around August–September, months before the presentation. The Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance issues the budget circular with instructions and formats to all ministries, States, UTs and autonomous bodies; departments prepare separate estimates of receipts and expenditure. The Finance Minister holds pre-budget consultations with State finance ministers and chief ministers, industry, farmers, social sector and labour representatives, NITI Aayog experts and economists.

The documents show Budget Estimates (BE) for the coming year, Revised Estimates (RE) for the current year, and Actuals for the year before. The AFS shows receipts and payments under three accounts: the Consolidated Fund of India, the Contingency Fund of India and the Public Account.
Budget speech: Part A covers the macroeconomic situation, priorities, total resources and sector-wise allocations and new schemes; Part B covers progress on policies and the tax proposals.

Documents laid besides the speech: the Annual Financial Statement, Demands for Grants, the Finance Bill, and statements required by the FRBM Act (Macro-Economic Framework Statement; Medium-Term Fiscal Policy cum Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement), plus nine explanatory documents. Expenditure "charged" on the Consolidated Fund (e.g. emoluments of the President, Supreme Court judges and heads of constitutional bodies) is not voted on and is shown separately.
In an election year a Vote on Account may first be taken for a few months, followed later by the full budget.
concepts.analogy: Preparing the budget is like a school annual day: rehearsals (circular and estimates) start months earlier; the show (presentation) happens on one fixed day; then the real work of running the year (execution) begins.
concepts.work: CAs working with government departments and PSUs prepare the departmental estimates that feed into the budget circular, and later track actual spending against BE and RE.

concepts.title: Presentation and enactment in Parliament
body: The budget is presented in the Lok Sabha on 1 February (since 2017-18, or another date the government decides); the railway budget was merged with the general budget from 2017-18. It is laid in the Rajya Sabha after the Finance Minister's speech.

Lok Sabha discussion has two stages: a general discussion on the whole budget; then, after an adjournment during which departmental standing committees examine the Demands for Grants, ministry-wise discussion and voting on the demands. The Lok Sabha may approve, reject or reduce a demand. The Rajya Sabha only discusses; it does not vote on demands.
Cut motions seek to reduce a demand — for economy, to express a policy difference or to voice a grievance.
Guillotine: on the last allotted day the Speaker puts all remaining demands to vote together, whether discussed or not, to finish within time.
Appropriation Bill: after voting on demands, it authorises withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India.

Finance Bill: introduced right after the budget presentation to give effect to tax proposals (imposition, abolition, alteration or regulation of taxes), with an explanatory memorandum. The motion for leave to introduce it cannot be opposed. It is taken up after the Appropriation Bill and must be passed within 75 days of introduction. As a money bill, the Rajya Sabha must return it within 14 days, with or without recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

blocks.title: Budget vocabulary

concepts.analogy: The Appropriation Bill is the permission to spend; the Finance Bill is the permission to tax.
concepts.work: Tax practitioners track the Finance Bill from introduction to enactment because amendments made in Parliament can change the final tax law clients must follow from 1 April.

concepts.title: Sources of revenue — receipts of the government
body: The Department of Revenue (Ministry of Finance) controls Union taxes through two statutory boards: the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT — income tax, corporation tax) and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC — GST, customs, central excise and other indirect taxes). It also administers laws on GST, central sales tax and stamp duties.

Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce an asset of the government. They are (a) tax revenue — corporation tax, taxes on income, wealth tax, customs, Union excise duties, GST including compensation cess, taxes of Union Territories; and (b) non-tax revenue — interest receipts, dividends and profits from public sector enterprises and surplus transferred by the RBI, other non-tax revenue (fees for social, economic and general services), and receipts of UTs.
Net tax revenue of the Centre = gross tax revenue − States' share − the National Calamity Contingent Duty transferred to the National Calamity Contingency Fund.

Capital receipts either create a liability or reduce an asset. (a) Non-debt capital receipts: recoveries of loans and advances; miscellaneous capital receipts such as disinvestment. (b) Debt capital receipts: market loans, short-term borrowings and treasury bills, securities issued against small savings, State provident funds (net), net external debt and other receipts (net) such as Sovereign Gold Bonds.

blocks.title: Classifying receipts

concepts.analogy: Revenue receipts are like your salary — yours to keep. Capital receipts are either a loan you must repay, or money from selling your old car (you are poorer by the car).
concepts.work: Disinvestment transactions — PSU share sales, offer for sale — involve CAs at every step; for the budget they are non-debt capital receipts that reduce the fiscal deficit.

concepts.title: Public expenditure management
body: Resources are limited, so total public spending must fit a sustainable macroeconomic framework. Developing economies need large public spending for growth and jobs, and cutting the fiscal deficit needs a clever mix of revenue and spending policies. Spending should reach socially desirable areas and deliver given outputs at minimum cost.
Unproductive spending leads to larger deficits, higher taxes, slower growth, fewer resources for other uses and a heavier future debt burden.

The Department of Expenditure is the nodal department for public financial management at the Centre and matters connected with State finances. It implements Finance Commission and Central Pay Commission recommendations, monitors audit observations, prepares Union accounts, and helps ministries control costs and prices of public services and improve procedures.

Pre-budget meetings chaired by the Secretary (Expenditure) discuss each ministry's needs; estimates are finalised after the Finance Minister approves. The "Expenditure Profile" (earlier called the Expenditure Budget) aggregates spending across ministries.

Classification: A. Centre's expenditure — establishment expenditure; central sector schemes (fully funded and run by Union agencies); other central expenditure including CPSEs and autonomous bodies. B. Transfers to States — Finance Commission transfers, centrally sponsored schemes and other transfers.

Revenue expenditure creates no physical or financial asset: running departments and services, interest payments, and grants to States and others (even if some grants are used for assets). Capital expenditure creates assets or reduces liabilities: land, buildings, machinery, investment in shares, loans and advances to States, UTs, PSUs and others.
concepts.analogy: Revenue expenditure is your monthly grocery and electricity bill; capital expenditure is buying a house or repaying your home loan.
concepts.work: Government auditors and CAs in PSUs classify every outflow as revenue or capital — a wrong classification distorts the revenue deficit reported to Parliament.

concepts.title: Types of budget and measures of deficit
body: Balanced budget: receipts = expenditure. Surplus budget: receipts > expenditure. Deficit budget: receipts < expenditure — it increases liabilities or reduces reserves; most modern economies run deficits.
Budgetary (overall) deficit: excess of total expenditure over total receipts, revenue and capital (in older usage, before counting new borrowing).
Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts. It shows that regular income cannot meet regular running costs, so the government borrows or diverts resources to pay for consumption.

Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings = (revenue expenditure + capital expenditure) − (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts). Equivalently FD = RD + (capital expenditure − non-debt capital receipts). It equals the government's total borrowing requirement and is usually expressed as a % of GDP. If RD forms a large share of FD, much of the borrowing is going into consumption, not investment.

Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − net interest liabilities (interest paid − interest received on domestic lending). It shows borrowing needed for purposes other than interest, i.e. the current-year imbalance. In simple problems where no interest receipts are given, interest payments are deducted directly.
Outcome budget: links allocations for schemes to measurable output and outcome targets — a progress card on how last year's money was used.

head: Measure
Formula
rows: Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts)
Revenue deficit + Capital expenditure − Non-debt capital receipts
blocks.title: Deficit formulas

concepts.analogy: Revenue deficit: your salary does not cover your monthly bills. Fiscal deficit: the total you must borrow this year. Primary deficit: what you would still need to borrow even if you had no old loans to pay interest on.
concepts.work: Rating agencies and bond desks read FD, RD and PD as % of GDP; CAs advising on G-sec investment or State bonds start from these ratios.

concepts.title: Public debt management
body: Public debt is debt contracted by the government against the Consolidated Fund of India, from internal and external sources — mainly market-based, fixed-rate domestic instruments used to finance the fiscal deficit. It must be repaid with interest; since some debt falls due every month, maturing bonds are usually refinanced by issuing new ones.

Public debt management means deciding the size and composition of debt, maturity pattern, interest rates and redemption, and implementing a strategy to raise funds at the desired cost and risk. The Centre's objective: meet financing needs at the lowest possible long-term cost, keep debt sustainable, and develop a deep domestic bond market. Its strategy rests on three pillars: low cost, risk mitigation and market development.

Institutions: RBI — domestic marketable debt (dated securities, treasury bills, cash management bills); its Internal Debt Management Department (IDMD) manages the domestic debt of the Centre, 28 State governments and two UTs. Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs) — external debt. Ministry of Finance Budget Division with RBI — other liabilities such as small savings, deposits and reserve funds. Treasury bills meet short-term cash needs; dated securities raise long-term funds. Since 1997 the RBI has given Ways and Means Advances (WMA) — temporary loans for a period of up to three months — to States that bank with it, to cover gaps between receipts and payments.

External debt comes mostly from multilateral agencies (IBRD, ADB); there is no sovereign borrowing from international capital markets; it is long-term and mostly at fixed rates; its main risk is rupee depreciation, which raises the cost of servicing.

FRBM Act, 2003 gives a legal framework to cut deficits and debt to sustainable levels. Objectives: inter-generational equity, long-run macroeconomic stability, better fiscal–monetary coordination and transparency in fiscal operations.

In 2016 a Public Debt Management Cell (PDMC) was set up within the Department of Economic Affairs, while a Medium-Term Debt Management Strategy (MTDS) sets the desired composition of debt. The RBI Retail Direct facility (announced 5 February 2021) lets retail investors open a G-sec account with the RBI and buy and sell government securities online.
Pandemic years (2020-21 and 2021-22) saw health and social spending rise while revenue fell, so the fiscal deficit and borrowing programme expanded sharply to provide counter-cyclical support.
concepts.analogy: Debt management is like a family rolling over its loans wisely: borrowing at the cheapest rate, spreading repayment dates so not everything falls due in one month, and avoiding loans in a foreign currency that could suddenly become expensive.
concepts.work: Treasury CAs in banks bid in RBI's G-sec and T-bill auctions; individuals can now buy G-secs via RBI Retail Direct — a product CAs often explain to clients.

concepts.title: The three government accounts
body: Consolidated Fund of India: every rupee of revenue, every loan the government raises and every repayment of loans it has given goes into this fund, and all government spending is paid out of it. Money can be spent only with Parliament's appropriation. It has revenue and capital divisions.

Contingency Fund of India: placed at the disposal of the President to give advances for urgent unforeseen expenditure without prior approval of Parliament; the amount is later reported to Parliament and recouped from the Consolidated Fund.

Public Account (Article 266(1)): funds where the government acts only as a banker — provident funds, small savings and similar deposits. The money belongs to depositors and must be returned, so spending from it does not need Parliament's approval.
concepts.analogy: Consolidated Fund = the family's main account (spending needs the elders' approval); Contingency Fund = the emergency cash in the drawer; Public Account = money a neighbour left with you for safe-keeping.
concepts.work: In government audits, CAs check that payments came from the right fund — for example that an urgent advance from the Contingency Fund was later recouped.

illustrations.title: Revenue, fiscal and primary deficit
illustrations.q: Budget data of a country (₹ crore): tax revenue 18,000; non-tax revenue 3,500; revenue expenditure 27,800 (including interest payments 6,200); capital expenditure 7,400; recovery of loans 600; disinvestment 900; borrowings 12,200. Compute revenue deficit, fiscal deficit and primary deficit, and the share of revenue deficit in fiscal deficit.

solution.text: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts = 27,800 − 21,500 = ₹6,300 crore.
Total expenditure = 27,800 + 7,400 = 35,200. Non-debt capital receipts = recovery of loans 600 + disinvestment 900 = 1,500.
Fiscal deficit = 35,200 − (21,500 + 1,500) = ₹12,200 crore — exactly the borrowings shown, as it must be.
Revenue deficit as % of fiscal deficit = 6,300 ÷ 12,200 × 100 = 51.64%: more than half of the borrowing is financing current (consumption) spending.
Borrowings are never deducted in computing the fiscal deficit — the fiscal deficit measures how much has to be borrowed.

checks.label: revenue deficit as % of fiscal deficit

illustrations.q: Classify: (1) dividend received from Coal India; (2) salaries of government staff; (3) loan given to a State; (4) proceeds from sale of shares of a PSU; (5) interest paid on G-secs; (6) construction of a highway; (7) grant to a State for building schools; (8) issue of treasury bills.

illustrations.title: Deficits as % of GDP, and the size of public debt
illustrations.q: A government's fiscal deficit is ₹16,00,000 crore and interest payments ₹12,50,000 crore; GDP is ₹3,50,00,000 crore. Find FD and PD as % of GDP. Also, Union debt (₹ crore) was: internal and other liabilities 1,90,43,590 and external 6,74,426 at 31 March 2026; 2,07,70,868 and 7,11,182 at 31 March 2027 (Budget 2026-27). Find total debt, its growth and the external share in 2027.

solution.text: Growth = (2,14,82,050 − 1,97,18,016) ÷ 1,97,18,016 × 100 = 8.95%. External share in 2027 = 7,11,182 ÷ 2,14,82,050 × 100 = 3.31% — India's public debt is overwhelmingly domestic.

jobs.title: Budget-day note for clients
jobs.situation: Your partner wants a two-page client note by the evening of 1 February.
steps: Read Part B of the speech and the Finance Bill memorandum for tax changes and their effective dates.
From the AFS and receipts budget, note FD, RD and PD as % of GDP and the borrowing programme.
Flag provisions effective from 1 April versus those effective immediately.
Mention that the Finance Bill may be amended before it is passed within 75 days.
jobs.takeaway: Knowing the budget documents tells you where each piece of information lives.
jobs.think: Why can a tax proposal in the budget speech still change before 1 April?
jobs.answer: The Finance Bill is debated and can be amended by the Lok Sabha before it is passed; only the enacted Finance Act binds.

jobs.title: Explaining G-secs to a retail client
jobs.situation: A retired client wants a safe investment and has heard about RBI Retail Direct.
steps: Explain that dated securities and T-bills are issued by the RBI on behalf of the government to finance the fiscal deficit.
Show how to open a Retail Direct account and bid non-competitively in auctions.
Explain interest-rate risk if sold before maturity.
jobs.takeaway: Public debt management has become a retail investment product.

jobs.title: Grant or capital?
jobs.situation: A department booked a grant to a municipal body for building drains as capital expenditure.
steps: Apply the rule that grants-in-aid are revenue expenditure of the giver, even if the receiver builds assets.
Recommend reclassification; note that the revenue deficit is understated as booked.
jobs.takeaway: Classification changes the reported revenue deficit — a figure Parliament and rating agencies watch closely.

mcqs.q: The constitutional provision requiring an "Annual Financial Statement" to be laid before Parliament is:
mcqs.explain: Article 112 — the word "budget" itself is not used in the Constitution.

mcqs.q: The Union budget is now normally presented on:
mcqs.explain: Advanced to 1 February from 2017-18.

mcqs.q: From which year was the railway budget merged with the general budget?
mcqs.explain: The merger took effect from the budget for 2017-18.

mcqs.q: The budget circular is issued by the:
options: Budget Division of the Ministry of Finance
mcqs.explain: Budget preparation starts in August–September with the Budget Division's circular.

mcqs.q: Part B of the Finance Minister's budget speech mainly contains:
options: Review of the macroeconomic situation only
mcqs.explain: Part A: economy and allocations; Part B: progress, policy direction and tax proposals.

mcqs.q: The Appropriation Bill is intended to:
options: Authorise withdrawal of money from the Consolidated Fund of India
mcqs.explain: The Finance Bill deals with taxes; the Appropriation Bill authorises spending.

mcqs.q: Within how many days of its introduction must Parliament pass the Finance Bill?
mcqs.explain: Finance Bill: 75 days; Rajya Sabha must return a money bill within 14 days.

mcqs.q: Putting all outstanding demands for grants to vote together on the last allotted day is called:
mcqs.explain: It brings financial debate to a close within time.

mcqs.q: A motion to reduce the amount of a demand for grant is a:
mcqs.explain: Cut motions may be for economy, policy disagreement or to voice a grievance.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Rajya Sabha and the budget is correct?
options: It discusses the budget but does not vote on demands for grants
It votes on every demand for grant
It can reject the Finance Bill
mcqs.explain: Only the Lok Sabha votes on demands; the Rajya Sabha can only recommend on money bills within 14 days.

mcqs.q: Direct taxes of the Union are administered by the:
mcqs.explain: CBDT — direct taxes; CBIC — GST, customs and excise.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a NON-tax revenue receipt?
options: Dividend and surplus transferred by the RBI
mcqs.explain: Dividends and profits of PSUs and the RBI surplus are non-tax revenue.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a non-debt capital receipt?
options: Disinvestment of government equity in a PSU
mcqs.explain: Recoveries of loans and disinvestment are non-debt capital receipts; the others create liabilities.

mcqs.q: Grants given by the Union to State governments are treated as:
mcqs.explain: Grants are revenue expenditure even if part is used by States to create assets.

mcqs.q: Loans and advances given by the Union to State governments are:
mcqs.explain: They create a financial asset for the Union.

mcqs.q: Fiscal deficit equals:
options: Total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings
Total expenditure − total receipts including borrowings
mcqs.explain: It shows the total borrowing requirement.

mcqs.q: Primary deficit equals:
mcqs.explain: It excludes the burden of past borrowing.

mcqs.q: Revenue receipts ₹21,500 crore; revenue expenditure ₹27,800 crore. Revenue deficit is:
Revenue receipts 24,000; recovery of loans 1,200; borrowings 16,300; other non-debt capital receipts 3,500; revenue expenditure 29,000; capital expenditure 16,000 (₹ crore). Fiscal deficit is:
mcqs.explain: FD = (29,000 + 16,000) − (24,000 + 1,200 + 3,500) = 16,300, which equals borrowings. ₹21,000 ignores all non-debt capital receipts; ₹19,800 ignores the other non-debt receipts; ₹5,000 is the revenue deficit.

mcqs.q: In the previous question, if interest payments are ₹4,100 crore (no interest receipts), the primary deficit is:
mcqs.explain: PD = 16,300 − 4,100 = 12,200. ₹20,400 adds interest instead of deducting it; ₹900 deducts interest from the revenue deficit.

mcqs.q: A large share of revenue deficit in fiscal deficit indicates that:
options: Borrowed funds are largely being used for consumption rather than investment
The government is creating many assets
mcqs.explain: Revenue deficit is borrowing to meet current (running) expenses.

mcqs.q: A surplus budget tends to:
mcqs.explain: Receipts exceed spending — more is withdrawn than injected.

mcqs.q: The domestic marketable debt of the Central and State governments is managed by the:
mcqs.explain: The RBI's Internal Debt Management Department manages it; external debt is with the Department of Economic Affairs.

mcqs.q: Ways and Means Advances given by the RBI to State governments are:
options: Short-term credit up to three months to bridge cash mismatches
Grants that need not be repaid
mcqs.explain: WMA (since 1997) cover temporary mismatches in receipts and payments.

mcqs.q: The FRBM Act was passed in:
mcqs.explain: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT an objective of the FRBM Act?
options: Guaranteeing a budget surplus every year
mcqs.explain: Its objectives are inter-generational equity, macro stability, fiscal–monetary coordination and transparency — not a yearly surplus.

mcqs.q: The main risk of the Government of India's external debt is:
options: Depreciation of the rupee raising servicing cost
Floating interest on most of it
Sovereign bonds issued in international markets
mcqs.explain: External debt is long-term, mostly fixed-rate, from multilaterals; currency depreciation is the main risk.

mcqs.q: Provident fund and small savings deposits held by the government are kept in the:
mcqs.explain: In the Public Account (Art. 266(1)) the government acts as banker; the money belongs to depositors.

mcqs.q: Urgent unforeseen expenditure before Parliament's approval is met from the:
mcqs.explain: Advances are made from the Contingency Fund and later recouped from the Consolidated Fund.

mcqs.q: The "Outcome Budget" mainly:
options: Links budget allocations to measurable outputs and outcomes
mcqs.explain: It is a progress card on how allocated money was used.

questions.q: From the following (₹ crore) compute revenue deficit, fiscal deficit and primary deficit (on net interest and on gross interest), and the share of revenue deficit in fiscal deficit: tax revenue 41,000; non-tax revenue 6,500 (including interest receipts 800); revenue expenditure 56,900 (including interest payments 9,800); capital expenditure 15,100; recovery of loans 1,200; disinvestment 2,300; borrowings 21,000.

model.text: Total expenditure = 56,900 + 15,100 = 72,000; non-debt capital receipts = 1,200 + 2,300 = 3,500. FD = 72,000 − (47,500 + 3,500) = ₹21,000 crore (= borrowings).
PD (net interest) = 21,000 − (9,800 − 800) = ₹12,000 crore; PD (gross interest) = 21,000 − 9,800 = ₹11,200 crore.

scheme.pt: Non-debt capital receipts identified; borrowings excluded
Fiscal deficit computed and reconciled with borrowings
RD share of FD with interpretation

remarks: Reconciling FD with borrowings is a quick self-check that examiners appreciate.
mistakes: Treating disinvestment as a revenue receipt.
Deducting borrowings in the FD formula.
tips: Write each formula in words before substituting numbers.

(Use gross interest payments for PD.)

Treating interest received as a capital receipt.

summary: Budget = statement of estimated receipts and expenditure; Article 112 calls it the Annual Financial Statement.
Stages: preparation (Aug–Sep circular by Budget Division) → presentation (1 Feb) and enactment → execution.
Lok Sabha: general discussion, standing committees, voting on demands (cut motions, guillotine) → Appropriation Bill → Finance Bill (75 days; Rajya Sabha 14 days).
Receipts: revenue (tax, non-tax) and capital (non-debt: loan recoveries, disinvestment; debt: borrowings). CBDT (direct), CBIC (indirect).
Expenditure: revenue (no asset; includes interest and grants) and capital (asset creation, loans given). Department of Expenditure is the nodal department.
RD = RE − RR; FD = TE − (RR + NDCR) = borrowing; PD = FD − net interest.
Debt: RBI/IDMD (domestic marketable), DEA (external), PDMC (2016), MTDS, WMA (since 1997, up to 3 months), FRBM 2003, RBI Retail Direct (5 Feb 2021).
Accounts: Consolidated Fund (needs appropriation), Contingency Fund (President; recouped), Public Account (Art. 266(1); government as banker).
remember: Vote on account in election years.
External debt: multilateral, long-term, fixed rate, no international bond issue; risk = rupee depreciation.
traps: Borrowings are not deducted in FD — FD equals borrowings.
Rajya Sabha cannot vote on demands.

quickref.v: (RE + CE) − (RR + recoveries of loans + disinvestment/other non-debt receipts) = borrowings
Fiscal deficit − net interest payments (interest paid − interest received)

viva.q: Define revenue deficit, fiscal deficit and primary deficit.
viva.model: Revenue deficit is revenue expenditure minus revenue receipts. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings, so it equals the total borrowing requirement. Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.

viva.q: Distinguish between revenue receipts and capital receipts with examples.
viva.model: Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce an asset of the government, for example taxes, dividends from public sector companies and fees. Capital receipts either create a liability or reduce an asset, for example borrowings, recovery of loans and disinvestment proceeds.

viva.q: Explain the roles of the Finance Bill and the Appropriation Bill.
viva.model: The Finance Bill gives effect to the tax proposals of the budget, that is imposing, abolishing or changing taxes, and Parliament must pass it within 75 days. The Appropriation Bill authorises the government to withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet expenditure.

viva.q: What are the Consolidated Fund, the Contingency Fund and the Public Account of India?
viva.model: The Consolidated Fund receives all revenues, loans raised and loan repayments, and all government expenditure comes out of it, but only with Parliament's appropriation. The Contingency Fund is at the disposal of the President for urgent unforeseen expenditure and is later recouped. The Public Account holds money like provident funds and small savings where the government is only a banker, so Parliament's approval is not needed to pay it out.

points.pt: Consolidated Fund — all revenue, loans; spending needs Parliament's appropriation
Contingency Fund — President; urgent unforeseen spending; recouped
Public Account — government as banker (PF, small savings)

viva.q: Who manages India's public debt, and what is the objective of debt management?
viva.model: The Reserve Bank of India, through its Internal Debt Management Department, manages the domestic marketable debt of the Centre and the States, such as dated securities and treasury bills. The Finance Ministry's Department of Economic Affairs looks after external debt. The objective is to meet the financing needs at the lowest long-term cost while keeping debt sustainable and developing the bond market.

viva.q: What is a guillotine and what is a cut motion in the budget process?
viva.model: A cut motion is a motion moved to reduce the amount of a demand for grant, for economy, policy difference or to voice a grievance. The guillotine is when, on the last day allotted, the Speaker puts all the remaining demands for grants to vote at once, whether discussed or not.
